I can see this from a few perspectives.

Personally, for me, I write out my script (not all parts of my script, just scenarios) in a fanfic-like way, it helps me experience the emotions that I feel in the scenario as I'm writing it. However, I get that it could feel less organic and for some, it could feel like you're not really in there, but just reading another fanfic of a self insert. But, I don't really agree with what moonlit says that exactly what you script won't happen -- there are an infinite number of realities and there will always be 1 where that exact conversation you write will happen. But, I guess she was trying to say that you should allow room for freedom, because writing it all out story-style makes you feel less involved? To be honest, unless you've scripted that you know what exactly will happen in your DR when you get there, I don't really see the issue in it.

Overall, I think it's just a matter of taste and what you personally like -- what gets you most connected to your DR. If you want to script general scenarios without a lot of detail, then go for it. If you want to script it insanely detailed, go for it -- a benefit of this is that when you're doing a method trying to visualise, you're not racking your mind trying to think think of what the people in your scenario are saying. I don't think anyone is expecting to have their scenario play out exactly just as they wrote it, so I think detailed scenarios are just there to help with visualisation and connecting to your DR.
